Ethos, Vision and Values
"Let your light Shine" Matthew 5:16
At Upton Noble Church of England VC Primary School we aspire to be: "A nurturing community of aspirational learners who flourish and grow together; building wisdom, knowledge and skills within a Christian ethos.”
Jesus taught that we can be the light and encourages us to let our light shine for all to see, reflecting the light of God.
We believe that by working together, we can grow the very best version of Upton Noble Church of England Primary School and
Our light will shine
By celebrating and nurturing the talents of all individuals in a safe learning environment, we will be able to be the best version of ourselves, valuing our own self-worth and
Our light will shine
By creating a culture of respect, resilience, friendship, honesty, trust and love, both within the school and the wider community, we can ignite and inspire curiosity and creativity, and
Our light will shine
Together, we nurture and encourage each other to develop resilience and perseverance, motivation and self-confidence, to become lifelong learners and
Our lights will shine
By peeling back the layers of understanding we develop a greater wisdom of life; little by little, deeper and deeper and day by day,
Our lights will shine brighter
When all our lights shine together anything is possible.
Our Christian values are at the core of everything we do.
They underpin our teaching and learning, and provide an environment which prepares our pupils as confident, happy citizens.

pageCache.pageTitle: Upton Noble C of E VC Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
On behalf of everyone here at Upton Noble Primary School, we are extremely proud to welcome you to our website.
Upton Noble Church of England VC Primary School is a small, welcoming village school set in the beautiful Somerset countryside, right in the heart of the county. The school benefits from school buses for our nearby villages - Batcombe, Brewham, Witham Friary and Wanstrow. The towns of Frome and Bruton are within easy reach.
We are proud to be a nurturing, family-orientated community where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish.
As part of a wider federation, we benefit from shared expertise, collaboration and strong leadership, while maintaining our unique identity and ethos.
Our school is built on a strong foundation of shared values that guide everything we do:
LOVE - RESILIENCE - FRIENDSHIP - RESPECT - TRUST - HONESTY
These values are not just words, they are lived daily through relationships, learning and the way we support one another.
We aim to develop children who are confident, compassionate and respectful, who strive to have a positive influence in the world.
We warmly welcome prospective families to visit our school, and we offer bespoke tours to share what makes our school a special place to be. If you would like more information or would like to visit, please contact us on: uptonnobleadmissions@eastsomersetfederation.co.uk
Mrs Rachael Bisset Executive Headteacher
"Pupils are eager to succeed and achieve well. They live up to the high ambitions that the school has for them." Ofsted, 2024

pageCache.text:
Maths Overview
Mathematics statement of Intent
At the East Somerset Federation, the teaching of mathematics aims to ensure that children are fluent in the fundamentals of the subject; are able to reason, both verbally and in writing; and are also able to solve problems in a range of contexts across the curriculum and in everyday life.
At the East Somerset Federation, we aim for every child to:
We follow the objectives as outlined in the national curriculum but use the White Rose Schemes of Learning to support our implementation of these objectives. We place considerable value on children having a secure understanding of the fundamentals of the subject and therefore use the Number Sense factual fluency programme to support this in KS1.
Following a mastery approach as endorsed by the DfE and the NCETM, our lessons use a range of practical resources and visual representations to support children's understanding of mathematical concepts. Children are routinely given opportunities to practise and consolidate on previously learned concepts as this is vital to move this knowledge into their long term memory.
We have 5 maths lessons per week in all classes, with each lesson 60 minutes long. In addition to this, children will regularly access 10 Tough Ten Maths arithmetic questions upon arriving to school. KS1 pupils will receive a 10 minute daily Number Sense session. In years 3 and 4 children will continue to develop their factual fluency with our schools times tables approach. Furthermore, children regularly practise their times tables at home using TT Rockstars and we have several whole school competitions annually.

pageCache.pageTitle: Upton Noble C of E VC Primary School - Computing Overview
pageCache.text:
Computing Overview
Welcome to our Computing page
Our Federation Computing Mission Statement
An excellent Computing education enable pupils to use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world. Computing has strong links with mathematics, science and design and technology, and provides insights into both natural and artificial systems. The core of computing is computer science, where pupils are taught the ideas of information and computation, how systems work and how to put this knowledge to use through programming.
Building on this, pupils are able to use information technology to create programs, systems and a range of content. Computing also ensures that pupils become digitally literate – able to use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through, information and communication technology – at a level suitable for the future workplace and as active participants in a digital world.
We use Teach Computing to deliver a range of exciting and motivating Computing lessons which challenge and inspire the children and we use ActiveBytes to deliver lessons to educate and encourage children to be Safer Online Citizens.
This is the overview of Computing in our school. The order of units may change to fit with what we are teaching in Quest. We teach a mixture of plugged and unplugged sessions which means that not all Computing sessions are on computers. This really helps children to plan, question, think and evaluate.
